imp.generic: She realized he hadn't actually said anything wrong.
imp.author: It was not, she presently came to feel, that he had said anything which a person of her own deliberate scruple could have fixed upon as wanting.

imp.generic: His politeness was actually a way of shutting her out.
imp.author: There were moments, indeed, when his perfect considerateness struck her as the subtlest form a withholding could assume.

imp.generic: The old man's silence wasn't anger, just withdrawal.
imp.author: What he had come, in the end, to recognise in the old man's silence was not, he should have been the first to insist, anything so coarse as displeasure; it was, if one were to be exact, a kind of large and patient withdrawal.

imp.generic: He understood it calmly, the way older people do.
imp.author: The knowledge came to him without bitterness, as such knowledge, at his age, was apt to come—rather, he reflected, as a faint coolness comes in at an opened door, perceptible only to those who had been warm.

imp.generic: She traveled to escape her problem, but it followed her.
imp.author: It was with something like consternation that she discovered the thing to have travelled with her—to be present, indeed, more vividly in the bright impersonal hotels than it had ever contrived to be at home.

imp.generic: The layout of the house kept people apart.
imp.author: The disposition of its rooms seemed to have been contrived—by what hand, and toward what end, he was at no early stage prepared to say—for the express purpose of keeping certain of its occupants forever just beyond the range of certain others.

imp.generic: He thought he was running things but he was being fooled.
imp.author: He, who had fancied himself the manager of the affair, came at last to suspect that he had been, from the threshold onward, no more than the most assiduous of its dupes.

imp.generic: For a second her calm slipped and I saw she was hopeful.
imp.author: The practised surface simply, for the space of a breath, was not there, and what looked through the gap—before the admirable discipline of years could reassemble itself—was a thing so young, so nakedly and unguardedly hopeful, that I have been ashamed ever since to have seen it.

imp.generic: She quickly composed herself and said the right thing.
imp.author: She recovered, of course; she said the right, the almost too perfectly right, thing; she even, a moment after, found within herself the resource of a small laugh against her own surprise.

imp.generic: Maybe you can never really leave your problems behind.
imp.author: She came to wonder whether what one fled were ever, in the nature of the case, the thing one had any real hope of leaving behind.
